title: Protocol for Generating Reproducible Miniaturized Controlled Midbrain Organoids
author: Chen, Niclis, et al.

steps.title: Prepare blocking solution
steps.instruction: Make a blocking solution containing 5 % donkey serum in PBS with 0.25 % Triton‑X.

steps.title: Collect MiCOs from EB‑Disk
steps.instruction: Place the EB‑Disk360 under a stereomicroscope on the flow bench, then use a P1000 pipette to withdraw MiCOs from the microwells; this can be performed at any desired time point for downstream assays such as immunostaining, HPLC, RNA or protein extraction.

steps.title: Immunostain MiCO sections
steps.instruction: Perform the following sequential treatments on mounted MiCO sections.

substeps.instruction: Permeabilize slides with PBT (0.25 % Triton X in PBS) for 10 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C).
Remove PBT and incubate with blocking solution (5 % donkey serum in PBT) for 1 h at room temperature (20‑25 °C).
Remove blocking solution; draw a circle around each section with a PAP pen, add primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution, and incubate at 4 °C overnight (16‑20 h).
Remove primary antibodies and wash slides 3 × 10 min with PBT.
Block again for 10 min with blocking solution.
Remove blocking solution and incubate with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature (20‑25 °C) in a humid, dark chamber.
Remove secondary antibodies and wash 3 × 10 min with PBT.
Remove PBT and incubate with DAPI (2‑(4‑Amidinophenyl)-6‑indolecarbamidine dihydrochloride) diluted in PBS for 5 min.
Remove DAPI and wash 3 × 5 min with PBS.
Remove PBS, mount slides with coverslips using DABCO.
Allow slides to dry under a fume hood in the dark, then store at 4 °C protected from light.
Image slides using a Zeiss LSM780 confocal microscope.

description: This protocol is focused on generating reproducible MiCOs without a necrotic center. We use this protocol to generate ventral midbrain (vmDA) MiCOs. We describe the specific steps for the generation of MiCOs starting directly from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) with the H9 line. However, we also used this protocol to generate MiCOs starting from the neural stem cell stage from widely used 2D protocols. The initial cell number per MiCO needs to be titrated.Alternatives: We have also used this protocol with an induced pluripotent stem cell line GBA-002-C3 (DANi-002C)1 and two genetically modified stem cell line generated in our lab.Note: When using different stem cell lines for midbrain dopaminergic differentiation, careful titration of the Wnt-agnoist CHIR99021 is necessary. For the H9 cells in our lab, we determined that 0.6 μM CHIR99021 is the optimal condition for dopaminergic neuronal differentiation. If the optimal CHIR99021 concentration for a cell line has been determined in a 2D system, this concentration can be used in this protocol. Alternatively, for more accurate midbrain patterning the CHIR99021 titration can be optimized directly in this protocol, by testing different CHIR99021 concentrations (0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 μM) in the culture media. The optimal concentration can be determined by the highest percentage of OTX2/EN1 double-positive cells and FOXA2/LMX1A double-positive cells.
